claims.claim: in 40 temperate lakes, convection exceeded wind shear in 18, including all 11 lakes smaller than 10 ha (cited as abstract)
claims.location: p. 1 (PDF p. 1), Abstract [1]; p. 4 (PDF p. 4), [13] and [19]
claims.quote: for 18 of the 40 lakes, including all 11 lakes <10 ha
claims.conditions: high-frequency buoy data from 40 temperate lakes (latitude 24.6–60°, 0.06 to > 64,000 ha); 'convection a larger source than wind shear' means the temporally averaged ratio u*/w* < 0.75 (Imberger 1985) over each lake's whole record; a sheltering coefficient was applied to the wind stress of the 14 smallest lakes
claims.note: The full text is now read, so '(abstract)' can be dropped.

claims.claim: convective k600 on cooling nights of 0.34–0.93 m/day at 25–200 W/m² of heat loss (Read et al. 2012, Tedford et al. 2014)
claims.conditions: Read et al.'s surface-renewal model; the heat-loss values, α = 2.2 × 10⁻⁴ K⁻¹ and ν = 0.955 × 10⁻⁶ m² s⁻¹ (22 °C water) are the project's (oxygen_metabolism.md §1); the paper itself gives no k for a stated heat loss
claims.note: With β = gαH/(ρc_p) (ρ 998, c_p 4,186): H = 25 W/m² gives β = 1.29 × 10⁻⁸ m² s⁻³, (βν)^¼ = 3.33 × 10⁻⁴ m/s, × 0.29 × 600^−½ = 3.94 × 10⁻⁶ m/s = 0.34 m/d; H = 200 gives 0.57 m/d. Read's constants therefore give 0.34–0.57 m/d; the upper 0.93 is Tedford et al.'s constants (0.5, 0.77·|β|) at 200 W/m², which this entry does not check. The comment should say the range spans the two parameterizations.

notes: Other values for the rewrite: the mean surface-renewal k for the 11 lakes < 10 ha was 0.54 m/d (SD 0.12), 'a conservative mean value' because η = 0.29 is the lower bound of Zappa et al. 2007 (p. 4 [18]–[19]); convection drove > 60 % of k in the six smallest lakes and up to 79 % in the smallest, 12–21 % in lakes > 10 km² (p. 4 [15]); w* peaks in late summer–early fall, u* in spring (Fig. 2). Hot Brook's lakes (Upper ~3 km²) fall between the small-lake and large-lake groups.
